beginner.summary: For developers, SREs and platform engineers who are new to distributed tracing with Jaeger. Covers the Jaeger v2 single binary built on the OpenTelemetry Collector, the all-in-one role with memory and Badger storage, the span and trace data model, sending OTLP spans from instrumented services, context propagation, the YAML configuration layout of receivers, processors, exporters and extensions, the Jaeger UI search, trace timeline, critical path, trace comparison and dependency graph, the HTTP query API, file-based sampling strategies, self-monitoring, and a traced three-service capstone.
prerequisites: Writes and runs small services in Python, Node.js, Java or Go and can read HTTP request logs
Uses Docker and Docker Compose to run containers, publish ports and read container logs
Uses curl and jq in a terminal to call HTTP APIs and filter JSON responses
outcomes: Run Jaeger v2 all-in-one with memory or Badger storage and confirm it receives OTLP spans
Instrument services with OpenTelemetry SDKs so their traces appear in Jaeger with correct parent-child links
Search, read, compare and export traces in the Jaeger UI and query them through the HTTP API
Use traces, the dependency graph and the critical path to locate the slow or failing service in a request

Administers Kubernetes, Kafka and at least one of Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Cassandra or ClickHouse in production
Writes PromQL alerts and reads Go service configuration and logs
outcomes: Control trace volume with adaptive sampling and tail sampling while keeping the traces teams need
Scale, secure and isolate a multi-tenant Jaeger platform across clusters with tested failure recovery
Tune storage backends and plan capacity and cost from measured span volumes
